description: Solo beginner team. Interested in game design and storytelling. Planning to submit a concept design for "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" (slides + voiceover), focusing on how players balance resources in a lunar/Mars outpost.
summary:
I developed a concept design for a decision-making game called "Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer." In this game, the player acts as the mission commander of a lunar or Mars outpost and must balance limited power, food, radiation shielding, and communication windows. Every choice has a cost, and the game shows the consequences over time.

This addresses the challenge by turning abstract engineering trade-offs into a playable experience. Instead of reading about why space missions are hard, players feel the difficulty of choosing between science instruments and fuel, or between stronger communication and lower power.

It is important because it can be used in STEM education to help students understand systems thinking—how one decision affects everything else. This skill applies beyond space, to engineering, business, and project planning.

This is a concept design presented as a 5-slide presentation. No coding was used. All values are simplified for educational purposes and are not actual NASA data.
details: This project is a concept design for a decision-making game called "Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer." The player acts as the mission commander of a lunar or Mars outpost and must make resource trade-offs: how much power goes to life support, how much food to grow, how much radiation shielding to bring, and when to send data back to Earth. Every choice has a cost, and the game shows the consequences over time. The goal is to keep the outpost alive and productive within real constraints, not to win a battle. The benefit is educational. Students learn systems thinking—how one decision affects everything else—and understand why real space missions are difficult, not because of technology alone, but because of limited resources and hard choices. The intended impact is to make space mission planning accessible and understandable for young learners. No coding languages or hardware were used. The project is a concept design presented as a 5-slide presentation created in Canva. The project is creative because it turns abstract engineering trade-offs into a playable decision-making experience, rather than a traditional quiz or lecture. As a solo beginner, I considered that the project must be simple, honest, and feasible without a technical background. All values are simplified for educational purposes and are not actual NASA data.
